questions.question: Define puberty, name the hormones involved, and list two changes that happen in both sexes, two only in girls and two only in boys.
questions.expected_answer: Puberty is the stage when a child's body develops into an adult body capable of reproduction. It is controlled by hormones: oestrogen (and progesterone) from the ovaries in girls and testosterone from the testes in boys, stimulated by hormones from the pituitary gland. Both: growth spurt; armpit and pubic hair; more sweat and body odour; oily skin and pimples; emotional changes. Girls: breasts develop; hips widen; menstruation starts. Boys: voice deepens; facial and body hair grows; shoulders broaden and muscles develop; sperm production begins.

questions.question: Name four organs of the male and four of the female reproductive system and give the function of each.
questions.expected_answer: Male: testes produce sperm and testosterone; scrotum holds the testes outside the body at a slightly lower temperature; sperm ducts carry sperm; prostate gland and seminal vesicles add fluid to form semen; urethra carries semen or urine out; penis delivers semen into the vagina. Female: ovaries contain eggs, release one each month and produce oestrogen and progesterone; oviducts carry the egg to the uterus and are where fertilisation takes place; uterus holds and nourishes a developing baby; cervix is the neck of the uterus; vagina receives sperm and is the birth canal.

questions.question: Describe the main events of a 28-day menstrual cycle and explain what happens if the egg is fertilised.
questions.expected_answer: Days 1 to about 5: menstruation, the uterus lining breaks down and leaves through the vagina. After that the lining thickens again. About day 14: ovulation, an egg is released from an ovary into an oviduct. The lining continues to thicken with blood vessels. If the egg is not fertilised it dies, the lining breaks down and menstruation begins a new cycle. If a sperm fertilises the egg in the oviduct, the zygote divides into a ball of cells, implants in the uterus lining about a week later, pregnancy begins, menstruation stops, and a placenta forms to supply food and oxygen and remove wastes through the umbilical cord for about nine months.
